newsitem.title: UK: Minimum 4.42 stg wage would help 26% of UK workers.
newsitem.headline: Minimum 4.42 stg wage would help 26% of UK workers.

text.p: A minimum wage of 4.42 stg per hour would help around 26 percent of the workforce, Britain's largest Trades Union UNISON said on Monday.
The union, which represent 1.3 million public sector workers, is asking Britain's new Labour government to impose a minimum wage of half the median male salary.
A rate of 4.42 stg, based on current earnings levels, would help 5.73 million workers and is equivalent to a weekly wage of 168 stg or 8,700 a year, a spokeswoman said.
Previous UNISON figures had been based on 4.26, half last year's median salary, and had suggest 24 percent of the workforce of 5.19 million would be helped.
In a report released earlier today, UNISON said there was a great need for a minimum wage following a huge increase in inequality during the 18 years the Conservatives were in power.

The Labour Party, which won the May 1 election, announced plans last week to set up a Low Pay Commission to take evidence from employers and workers' representatives before recommending a new minimum wage.
UNISON has pledged to keep up the pressure for a decent minimum rate which would make a real difference to workers on low pay.
